result.journal: Proc. ACM Meas. Anal. Comput. Syst.
result.keywords: Modern monitoring and adversarial measurement systems increasingly rely on efficient sketch-based summaries that can support multiple queries over restricted time windows. In this article, we combine interval-aware telemetry with an analysis of covert signal leakage in power-sensitive desktop environments. We propose a unified framework that allows operators to issue drill-down tasks such as heavy hitter detection, entropy estimation, and burst localization for specific periods of interest, while also characterizing how switching-noise patterns can be leveraged for stealthy information transfer across a building's electrical network. Our study presents accuracy guarantees for the telemetry component, evaluates robustness under realistic load variation, and demonstrates how timing- and frequency-based observations can be correlated to identify anomalous activity without intrusive instrumentation. We further discuss practical mitigations including filtering, scheduling, and traffic shaping, along with their limitations.
result.title: Silent Interval, Hidden Ripple: Adaptive Telemetry and Covert Exfiltration in Power-Aware Networks.
